methodology.UserFees: Traders pay each pool's configured swap fee, read on-chain per pool (ranges roughly 0.01%–0.25%).
methodology.Fees: Total swap fees charged to traders, using each pool's on-chain fee rate.
methodology.Revenue: Half of the swap fees (the pool admin fee); the other half stays with liquidity providers.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: Treasury keeps 10% of swap fees (20% of the admin fee).
methodology.HoldersRevenue: 40% of swap fees (80% of the admin fee) funds CAKE buyback and burn.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: Liquidity providers keep 50% of swap fees (the non-admin half).

methodology.Volume: Everything staked on the up and down sides of every five-minute round, across the BNB, BTC and ETH price markets.
methodology.NotionalVolume: The size of each round's pot, which is what gets paid out when the round settles. Both sides stake into the same pot, so this matches the amount staked.
methodology.Fees: 3% of each round's total pot, counting both the winning and the losing stakes, taken when the round settles. When a round ends with nobody to pay out - the price finishes exactly where it started, or every bet was on the losing side — the whole pot goes to the treasury instead.
methodology.Revenue: All of the fee is kept. Winners are paid out of the losing stakes, so there are no liquidity providers or market makers taking a share.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: Zero. Everything the treasury collects is spent on buying back and burning CAKE, so none of it is retained.
methodology.HoldersRevenue: All the revenue goes to CAKE buyback and burn

Fees.Prediction Fees: 3% of each round's total pot, taken when the round settles, or the whole pot when a round ends with no winners

Revenue.Prediction Fees To Holders: All the fee is kept as revenue, it will be used to buy back and burn CAKE

HoldersRevenue.Buy Back And Burn CAKE: All the revenue goes to CAKE buyback and burn
